messages:
Omar: quick check — onboarding tempest14b v2: weights landed at s3://redwood-models/tempest/14b/v2/merged-quant.pt. Can someone confirm the loader will accept this path? I noticed older uploads use a /weights/ prefix.
Liz: pulled the manifest — our current loader expects s3://.../weights/<file>. We do have a redirect in model-registry, but runtime prefetch uses prefix matching which will miss the new object unless we copy or support either prefix.
Omar: prefer avoiding extra S3 copies. Kevin, any objection to loader accepting both prefixes? @kevin
Kevin: I can add tolerant prefix parsing today. Opening a small PR. One thing I found: tokenizer_meta.json shows "tokenization": "gpt2" but the vocab files are sentencepiece. That's a mismatch — runtime gpt2-mode will map eos differently and can cause early truncation.
Ashley: yep that's the tokenizer quirk I flagged earlier. If runtime decodes with the wrong tokenizer, we'll see premature <eos> and length drops. Need a smoke decode test.
ci-bot: run decode-smoke for model tempest14b/v2 — status: passed. Sample length 512 ok, but secondary stress run logged early <eos> at ~230 on a list-generation prompt.
Liz: CI smoke pass is fine but stress tests show truncation when continuous batching >8. I think scheduler batching + cached KV from earlier prefixes plus tokenizer mismatch are interacting.
Kevin: proposed serving config tweak for preflight and canary:
```
continuous_batching:
  min_batch_size: 1
  max_batch_size: 8
  max_wait_ms: 12
kv_cache:
  policy: "prefix-aware"
  prefetch: true
  max_prefetch_bytes: 10485760
max_tokens: 2048
```
Omar: "prefix-aware" kv_cache — do we have that implemented? If not, that's a risky opt.
Liz: not fully implemented. I can add a scheduler guard: on request start, compare model.tokenizer.name to runtime.session.tokenizer.name; if mismatch, temporarily disable KV reuse for that session. Cheap and safe.
Ashley: also need to validate max_tokens: model metadata claims 4096, but weights were trimmed and tokenizer vocab suggests shorter effective context. Add an onboarding validation: decode + token count check vs declared max.
Kevin: creating PRs now: loader prefix handling (WIP), tokenizer_meta fix (WIP), scheduler guard (WIP). I'll tag reviewers.
Omar: assign to me for final validation after PR merges. Also ops-bot kicked a canary earlier at 1998754335.
ops-bot: canary deploy started: cluster inference-canary-7, image runtime:canary-2026-03-17. Health: 3/3 passing.
Liz: once loader + tokenizer fixes land, can we run a preflight that:
- downloads weights from loader-resolved S3 path
- validates tokenizer mapping (eos, unk, pad tokens)
- runs 1k vectorized requests with continuous_batching=16 then 8
- checks early-eos rate <1% and p90 latency within SLO
Ashley: I'll add that script and hook it into the model-registry preflight and tie it to the PRs.
Kevin: PR links: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/4823 (loader tolerant path), https://git.internal/redwood/model-registry/pull/991 (tokenizer_meta fix), https://git.internal/redwood/scheduler/pull/210 (kv guard)
Omar: thanks. I'll wait for CI and then run the preflight validation and weight sanity. Ping here when the canary has a 30m extended run.
Liz: ping me once extended canary run completes and preflight results are green. :thumbsup:
